items.title: perf(ui): reclaim Chat boot bytes and lower budgets (#194135)
items.summary: perf(ui): reclaim Chat boot bytes and lower budgets (#194135) * perf(ui): reclaim Chat boot bytes and lower budgets Remove retired English copy, obsolete browser fallbacks, and unused emitted initialization. Preserve layout and behavior while reducing normalized Chat boot by 1,741 B and total CSS by 158 B; ratchet measured caps with 64 B headroom. * fix(ui): preserve Communications tab spacing * test(ui): scope catalog idle checks to the current socket * perf(ui): ratchet caps against complete plugin builds * fix(ui): cancel scheduled sidebar captures on deletion Retire a pending timer or idle capture when snapshot invalidation removes a session. Otherwise a cross-tab deletion can be followed by a stale live projection that writes the deleted row back into storage before the local roster catches up. Keep the two-tab write budget unchanged. Add a persisted-row regression that fails before the fix; all 34 owner tests and both deletion E2E cases pass. The repair adds 3 B normalized gzip and retains a 1,829 B Chat boot saving; ratchet caps to the final measurements plus 64 B. * test(ui): settle menu entry animation before spacing checks WebKit CI observed the menu's 0.95 entry scale, turning the correct 6px gap into a transient 5.7px rectangle gap. Finish finite menu animations with the existing helper before measuring static geometry; retain the exact spacing, clickability, and modal assertions. All nine transient surface cases pass in Chromium and WebKit. UI types, focused lint/format, and independent review pass. Production bundles are unchanged. * test(ui): allocate sidebar regression coverage Record the 11 net test lines for the persisted-row resurrection regression and native-menu geometry settlement after removing redundant base64 fallback coverage. Keep the shared test-line scalar unchanged. The exact test-line ratchet and independent review pass. This is metadata only; production assets and prior behavior proof are unchanged. * test(ui): await queued catalog publications before picker checks Track observed catalog invalidations until the corresponding read starts, then retain the existing reply and no-new-request assertions. This covers the publication coalescing window without arbitrary sleeps or product changes. The scoped test allocation now covers 27 net regression-test lines, including 16 lines for publication settlement.

items.title: fix(macos): Dashboard widgets fail to load over Remote over SSH (#193…
items.summary: fix(macos): Dashboard widgets fail to load over Remote over SSH (#193854) * fix(macos): forward the widget sandbox port over Remote over SSH The SSH tunnel forwarded only the Gateway port, so Dashboard widgets and MCP Apps could not reach the remote sandbox listener (Gateway port + 1) that the Control UI addresses on the tunnel host. Forward it to the same local port, skipping it when that port is busy or reserved by a Gateway this Mac hosts. Refs #145522 * fix(macos): reserve local sandbox ports only while hosting is on Turning hosting beside the remote primary off keeps the separated gateway.port, so the port split no longer implies a local Gateway. Read the hosting preference instead; it stays part of the tunnel configuration, so toggling it replaces the tunnel and frees or claims the port. Refs #145522 * fix(macos): retire a stale SSH tunnel before starting the hosted Gateway A tunnel opened while hosting was off can hold the hosted Gateway's port or its widget sandbox port. Local startup attached to that listener and skipped launching, and the later tunnel replacement never reran startup. Retire a tunnel whose configuration is stale, and wait for its SSH process to exit, before starting the hosted Gateway. Refs #145522 * fix(macos): replace an SSH tunnel missing its widget sandbox forward A tunnel opened while the sandbox port was busy or reserved (a hosted Gateway still shutting down, a stale tunnel) stayed healthy and reusable for as long as its control port listened, so widgets stayed unreachable after the port freed. Record the forward each tunnel actually opened, and have the manager's reuse check replace a tunnel without it once that port is available. Refs #145522 * fix(macos): run the widget sandbox forward in its own SSH process Both forwards shared one ssh process with ExitOnForwardFailure, so a sandbox bind failure took the Gateway route down, and the reuse check retired a healthy Gateway tunnel to add the forward. The probe also bound loopback with SO_REUSEADDR, which succeeds beside a 0.0.0.0 listener that ssh then collides with (GatewayPorts=yes) or shadows. Open the sandbox forward in a separate ssh process owned by the tunnel manager, retried at most every 30 s and retired with the Gateway route. Pin it to 127.0.0.1 so ssh_config cannot move the bind, and probe that address without SO_REUSEADDR so any existing listener counts as busy. Refs #145522 * fix(macos): log skipped widget sandbox forwards and describe their retry Log once per route when the sandbox port is in use or reserved, describe the lookup-driven retry with its 30 s backoff in the docs, and name the manager fixture test for what it proves. Refs #145522 * fix(macos): cancel an unfinished widget sandbox forward on retirement * fix(macos): keep the widget sandbox forward recognizable to shipped PortGuardian v2026.11.1 shares the version 2 PortGuardian ledger and drops any receipt whose ssh command it cannot match before it checks the live parent. The explicit 127.0.0.1 bind address on the sandbox forward was such a command, so a running stable app could erase the receipt of this build's live forward. Use the Gateway tunnel's -L shape and pin the loopback bind with a command-line GatewayPorts=no, and keep the matcher identical to stable. * fix(macos): keep inherited alias forwards from ending the widget sandbox forward The sandbox SSH process reads the same ssh alias as the Gateway process. Any LocalForward, RemoteForward or DynamicForward in that alias is already held by the Gateway process, so the sandbox copy always failed to bind and ExitOnForwardFailure=yes ended the sandbox process on every retry, even with its own port free. ClearAllForwardings would also clear the sandbox -L. Turn ExitOnForwardFailure off for the sandbox process only. Readiness already requires this pid to listen on the sandbox port, so a failed own bind still ends the attempt. The Gateway command is unchanged.

items.title: NTT Docomo線上服務遭駭，可能洩露30萬筆用戶個資
items.summary: 日本行動電信NTT Docomo本週公告網站及My docomo服務遭到駭客攻擊，可能有多達30萬筆用戶個資外洩，包括電話號碼等資料。 NTT Docomo在11月4日確認Docomo線上商店及My docomo服務遭到第三方人士未經授權存取。為防止損害擴大及進行調查，Docomo在11月5日凌晨1時5分左右暫停Docomo線上商店及My docomo的各項手續。這些服務可供用戶查詢合約內容、辦理合約異動及購買手機等產品。
